message.content:
**C♯ Major Scale**

| Degree | Note |
|--------|------|
| I      | C♯   |
| ii     | D♯   |
| iii    | E♭   (or F♭) – enharmonically equivalent to D♮ but traditionally written as E♭ in this context |
| IV     | F♯   |
| V      | G♯   |
| vi     | A♯   |
| vii°   | B♭   (or C♭) – enharmonic to B natural; often written as B♭ in theoretical contexts |

In standard notation, the **C♯ major** scale consists of the following pitches:

```
C♯ - D♯ - E♯(F) - F♯ - G♯ - A♯ - B♯(C)
```

Because it contains seven sharps (including the double‑sharp on B), it’s one of the most complex keys in terms of accidentals. In practice musicians may use its enharmonic counterpart, **D♭ major**, which has five flats instead.
